abstract: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women worldwide. Many breast cancers originate from the cells lining the milk duct and some become invasive. Breast cancer lacking estrogen, progesterone receptors (ER-, PR-) and epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2-) amplification, termed “Triple negative” (TNBC) is reported to frequently affect Black women and younger women. TNBC is an invasive ductal carcinoma with limited treatment options. To this end, we opted to investigate drugs that could be repurposed because they offer advantages in bringing effective treatments faster to the clinic. We chose to study the effect of the drug, dapivirine, a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) of HIV because it could be detected in the breast milk of lactating women when treated for HIV and the drug could potentially target the cancer. Here we show the potent impact of dapivirine on MDA-MB-231 TNBC cells, while NNRTI like nevirapine showed marginal effects. When dapivirine was tested on other breast cell lines, MCF-7 and MCF 10A, the inhibition was at higher concentrations. Molecular studies with dapivirine in TNBC cells, revealed an increase in reactive oxygen species (ROS), apoptotic cells, and activation of caspases. Importantly, protein profiling and STRING analysis revealed deregulation of the key molecule, PCNA and impact on pivotal cell signaling circuits including extracellular matrix (ECM), angiogenesis, cell adhesion, and immunomodulation. Of note, is its potential effect on stem-like cells due to downregulation of the basic transcription factor 3 (BTF3) and proteasome activator complex subunit 3; the latter affecting their dependence on the proteasome pathway. Taken together, dapivirine exhibits the potential to be considered as a repurposed drug for TNBC as monotherapy/combination therapy. Notably, it could also potentially be a treatment for individuals with dual ailments, such as HIV and TNBC, if the clinical outcomes with dapivirine for TNBC become favorable. Supplementary Information The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1038/s41598-024-79789-y.
methods:
Methods
Cell lines and materials
Dapivirine was purchased from Selleckchem (Houston, TX, USA). A 50 mM stock solution was prepared in DMSO and stored at – 20 °C until use. Reagents for flow cytometry were purchased from Cytek Biosciences (Fremont, CA, USA).
MDA-MB-231 cell line was purchased from American Type Culture Collection (ATCC, USA). MDA-MB-231 cells were grown in L-15 medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin and 2 mM glutamine. Cultures were incubated at 37 °C in the absence of CO
2
. MCF-7 and MCF 10A cell lines were also purchased from ATCC. MCF-7 cells were cultured in Eagle’s minimal essential medium (EMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin (P/S) and 2 mM glutamine. MCF 10A cells were grown in DMEM/F12 supplemented with 5% horse serum, EGF (20 ng/ml), Hydrocortisone (0.5 µg/ml), Insulin (10 µg/ml), Non-essential amino acids (1%) and P/S (1%). Both MCF-7 and MCF 10A cell lines were maintained at 37 °C in a 5% CO
2
atmosphere.
Assessment of the effect of dapivirine on the viability of MDA-MB-231 cells
The assays were performed as described earlier
69
. Essentially, MDA-MB-231 cells were plated in 96-well plates at a density of 5000 cells per well. After 24 h, cells were treated with varying concentrations of dapivirine in triplicates and incubated for 72 h at 37 °C. Cell viability was assessed by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) (Bimake, Houston, TX, USA). The media was aspirated, and 200 µL of 20% CCK-8 solution in the complete growth medium was added. Absorbance was measured at 450 nm using an Infinite 200Pro plate reader (Tecan, USA) after 1.5 h of incubation at 37 °C. The viability of cells was expressed after normalizing the treatment group absorbance values to that of the control group. Using Prism software, version 7.0 (GraphPad, USA), graphs were generated and IC
50
was determined. Three independent experiments were performed.
Immunofluorescence labelling
Cells were plated in glass chamber slides at a density of 20,000 cells/well. After 24 h, they were treated with 1 µM, 2 µM and 5 µM of dapivirine for 72 h. Thereafter, cells were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min and washed twice with PBS, each for a minute. Cells were permeabilized with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 5 min followed by application of fluorescent labeled phalloidin (Actin Red 555 ReadyProbes Reagent, Invitrogen
R37112
) for 10 min at room temperature as per manufacturer’s instructions and washed twice in PBS for 1 min each time.
Clonogenic assays
These assays were performed essentially as described earlier
69
. MDA-MB-231 cells treated with varying concentrations of dapivirine were trypsinized and replated at a density of 500 cells/well in 6-well plates in the growth medium. Cells from untreated cultures served as controls. The assays were done in triplicates. After 10 days of incubation, cultures were fixed and stained with crystal violet. Quantitative estimation was made by lysing the colonies by adding 1% SDS and measuring the absorbance at 590 nm.
Flow cytometric analysis
Flow cytometric assays were performed essentially as described
70
. MDA-MB-231 cells were plated in 12-well plates at 62,500 cells/well. After 24 h, cultures were treated in triplicate for 72 h with 1 µM, 2 µM and 5 µM concentrations of dapivirine. Cultures with only media served as controls. After 72 h of incubation, cultures were trypsinized and cells were pooled together from triplicate treatments before proceeding with flow cytometry assay kit protocol as per manufacturer’s instructions (Cytek Biosciences, Fremont, CA, USA). The following Luminex Muse assay kits were used: Oxidative Stress kit (MCH100111), Annexin V and dead cell kit (MCH100105), MultiCaspase kit (MCH100109), Caspases 3/7 (MCH100108).
Proteomic analysis
Protein profiling was performed by first running 2-D DIGE, followed by Mass spectrometry by Applied Biomics Inc. (Hayward, CA, USA). Basically, the following procedures were employed for the protein profiling. Cells were plated (62,000 cells/well) in 12-well plates. Cells were treated at 3.5 µM dapivirine and untreated controls were maintained in parallel. After 72 h, cells from control samples and treated samples were collected, washed with 1× PBS, and then stored at −  80 °C prior to sending the samples to Applied Biomics, Inc (Hayward, CA, USA) on dry ice for proteomic analysis. The protocol performed was as described previously
70
–
72
. STRING database version 12.0 was used to perform functional enrichment analysis and to generate protein-protein interaction networks
73
.

Dapivirine was purchased from Selleckchem (Houston, TX, USA). A 50 mM stock solution was prepared in DMSO and stored at – 20 °C until use. Reagents for flow cytometry were purchased from Cytek Biosciences (Fremont, CA, USA).
MDA-MB-231 cell line was purchased from American Type Culture Collection (ATCC, USA). MDA-MB-231 cells were grown in L-15 medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin and 2 mM glutamine. Cultures were incubated at 37 °C in the absence of CO
2

MCF-7 cells were cultured in Eagle’s minimal essential medium (EMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin (P/S) and 2 mM glutamine. MCF 10A cells were grown in DMEM/F12 supplemented with 5% horse serum, EGF (20 ng/ml), Hydrocortisone (0.5 µg/ml), Insulin (10 µg/ml), Non-essential amino acids (1%) and P/S (1%). Both MCF-7 and MCF 10A cell lines were maintained at 37 °C in a 5% CO

Introduction
The most common malignancy occurring in women worldwide is cancer of the breast
1
,
2
. In many cases, breast cancers originate from the cells lining the milk duct, and are classified as ductal carcinomas
3
. When these cells become invasive, they are then categorized as invasive ductal carcinomas. Among the breast cancers, TNBC forms 10–15% of the cancers identified and is known to be heterogeneous; importantly, it is also more aggressive than other breast cancers
4
. Breast cancer with TNBC phenotype presents as an invasive ductal carcinoma and also exhibits biological variations
5
. Treatment options for TNBC are limited because they do not respond to hormonal therapies unlike other types of breast cancers; thus, TNBC is typically treated with chemotherapy. Although TNBC is considered chemosensitive, the cancer relapse rate is high due to its aggressive nature when compared to other breast cancers and assays for precision medicine have been reported
6
,
7
. While it can occur in anyone, the frequency of occurrence in Black women as well as younger women is higher. Considering that efficacious treatment options are limited for TNBC, novel therapeutic options are warranted
8
,
9
.
Recent advances in chemotherapy, and treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors have led to better outcomes when assessed during the early stages of TNBC, but efficacious treatments are very much needed
9
. Importantly, cell types of TNBC have been reported to express changes in pivotal cell pathways: entities affecting metastasis including cell adhesion properties, interactions at the ECM-receptor stage, and angiogenesis
10
. Further, it has been reported that TNBC belongs to a diverse group with varied molecular subtypes
11
. Targeted therapeutics toward these metastatic pathways and agents causing cellular and molecular anomalies could provide potential novel and better treatment options for TNBC.
We opted to identify compounds that could be repurposed because repurposing/repositioning of drugs that are already in the clinic for new indications is considered an option that offers valuable advantages like bringing treatments faster to the clinic
12
, which is very much needed for a malady like TNBC. To this end, we chose to investigate the effect of dapivirine, a HIV NNRTI on TNBC cells (utilizing the MDA-MB-231 cell line) because it was detected and quantified in the breast milk of lactating women with HIV when treated with this inhibitor
13
,
14
.
Dapivirine is a substituted diarylpyrimidine analog and belongs to the low molecular weight NNRTIs for HIV treatment. Further, when tested at 1mM over a 24 h period on ex vivo cervical tissue explants, dapivirine did not exhibit significant toxicity
15
. Well-established preclinical models to test novel drugs affecting various pathways for TNBC are lacking, although substantial advancement has been made based on targeting certain entities such as WEE1 and BCL-XL of TNBC
16
; other inhibitors of various pathways controlling TNBC are yet to be studied in this model system. In the syngeneic mice model
17
, which is also instrumental as a TNBC preclinical model, assessment of drug effects has not been investigated and further experimentation is suggested. In the absence of a well-established in vivo model system to study the effect of novel compounds on TNBC, we performed in-depth analysis (cellular, molecular, and proteomics) with the HIV inhibitor, dapivirine, using the TNBC cell line MDA-MB-231, to elucidate its mechanism of action and identify potential target molecules that could be considered as novel treatment options for TNBC, an aggressive malady.
Results
Dapivirine impacts the viability of breast cancer cells
To evaluate the anticancer potential of dapivirine on breast cancer cells, various breast cancer cell lines were utilized for the experiment: MDA-MB-231 (representing TNBC), MCF-7 (ER + and invasive in nature), MCF 10A (a non-tumorigenic cell line); the cells from these cell lines were treated with various concentrations of the drug. A significant impact on the viability of MDA-MB-231 cells on treatment with dapivirine was observed. Further, a dose-dependent response with a sharp decline in viability between 1µM and 5 µM was observed in these cells when compared to other breast cancer cell lines, Fig.
1
A, with an IC
50
of 3.5 μM, while it was > 10 µM for MCF-7 and only marginal inhibition was observed in MCF 10A cells. On observing the potent inhibition of viability of MDA-MB-231 cells by dapivirine, we examined its effect on the cell morphology by staining the cells with rhodamine (ActinRed 555). Images of rhodamine-stained MDA-MB-231 control cells and dapivirine-treated cells (at various concentrations of dapivirine) are shown, Fig.
1
B. As seen in the images, the dapivirine-treated MDA-MB-231 cells exhibited altered morphology; they look flat and spread out and are few in number when compared to the control cells. Further, to assess the effect of dapivirine on colony-forming ability, clonogenic assays were performed at various concentrations of dapivirine. Dapivirine impacted the ability of the treated cells to form colonies, thus affecting the proliferation potential of MDA-MB-231 cells, Fig.
1
C. Moreover, when compared to the control cells, treated cells exhibited sustained response even after withdrawal of the drug, Fig.
1
D. On observing the impact of dapivirine on MDA-MB-231 cells, we opted to investigate the effect of another HIV NNRTI drug, nevirapine which is currently administered in the clinic. The viability assay in the presence of nevirapine was performed identically to that performed in the presence of dapivirine. Nevirapine exhibited marginal effect with IC
50
values much higher than dapivirine as shown in Fig.
1
E.

Extrinsic programmed cell death pathway was activated by dapivirine in MDA-MB-231 cells

For assessing the extrinsic programmed cell death pathway, Annexin V flow cytometric assay was performed. Cells were treated with various concentrations (1 µM, 2 µM, and 5 µM) of the drug and incubated at 37 °C for 72 h. Representative scatter plots are shown in Fig.
2

2

Dapivirine increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in MDA-MB-231 cells
On observing the induction of apoptosis and activation of caspases in MDA-MB-231 cells by dapivirine, we investigated whether changes in ROS levels have occurred in these cells. The production of superoxide radicals in dapivirine-treated cells was quantitatively measured using the well-optimized reagent, dihydroethidium, which is used to detect ROS. To determine cell populations of MDA-MB-231 cells that have increased ROS levels, flow cytometry was performed using the oxidative stress kit at the IC
50

Discussion
In an attempt to discover novel compounds that could inhibit TNBC cells, we directed our efforts towards identifying compounds that could be repurposed because repurposing drugs known for other ailments could reduce the timeline of bringing them to the clinic as the safety and toxicity assessments are completed
12
. Also, this would expedite drug discovery for the much-needed treatment for a cancer like the triple negative breast cancer which has very few therapeutic options. We chose the HIV NNRTI, dapivirine because it could be detected and quantified in the breast milk of lactating women with HIV when treated with this drug
13
,
14
.
In the present study, we conducted multilevel analysis to investigate the impact of dapivirine on the TNBC cell line MDA-MB-231. Cellular level analysis showed potent inhibition of cell viability and proliferation potential of TNBC cells at an IC
50
concentration of 3.5 µM. Further, elucidation of the molecular mechanism of action revealed an impact on the extrinsic programmed cell death pathway with an increase in the number of apoptotic, multicaspase, and executioner 3/7 caspases. Importantly, there was a significant increase in the levels of ROS which could have led to the activation of the programmed cell death pathway that we observed. It is reported that elevation in ROS levels particularly in cancer cells can lead to their death via signaling pathways including apoptosis
18
. The increase in ROS observed in the molecular assay in dapivirine-treated cells could be one of the causes for inhibition observed in MDA-MB-231 cells via the apoptotic pathway. Future studies also need to explore the impact of dapivirine on cell cycle progression.
To investigate further the potent action of dapivirine, we performed highly sensitive assays like 2D-DIGE and mass spectrometry which can detect molecules in the femtomolar range
19
. Various entities of key cellular pathways were differentially regulated. One of the upregulated entities was hypoxia up-regulated protein 1. It has been reported that when TNBC cells are under stress, including endoplasmic reticulum stress, due to unfolded protein response (UPR), the spliced form of X-box-protein1 (XBPI-s ) is activated which regulates the hypoxia up-regulated protein 1 driven transcriptional network
20
. If resistance arises, inhibitors of UPR along with dapivirine would be a beneficial option as a combination treatment strategy. In fact, a small molecule, BHPI (3,3-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)-7-methyl-1,3-dihydro-2H-indol-2-one), has been reported to counteract the protective role of UPR by its sustained presence leading to regression of breast cancer cells
21
.
Endoplasmin was also one of the upregulated entities in the present study. Endoplasmin, also called gp96, HSP90 is a chaperone protein residing in the endoplasmic reticulum. It is known to play a key role in innate and adaptive immunity and is considered an immune chaperone. Notably, gp96 is known to induce immunity to antigens from the cells from which it has been derived and unlike other ER proteins, it shows specific immunogenicity
22
. Notably, it is reported that in breast tumors, gp96 is expressed on the surface of the malignant tumors, but not in nonmalignant tumors
23
. Therefore, it could form an attractive target for the treatment of TNBC as specific antigenic immune responses could occur, just like it is reported for other tumors including glioblastomas
24
. Therefore, upregulation of this pivotal moiety in TNBC cells on treatment with dapivirine could potentially aid in developing an effective chemo-immunotherapy for this highly aggressive form of cancer.
Calreticulin (CRT), is an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) residing protein and is known to translocate to the plasma membrane as a result of ER stress-related apoptosis leading to immunogenic cell death (ICD). ICD is induced by various agents and conditions
25
including the action of anticancer agents like doxorubicin (DOX), which results in Ecto-CRT and this is an “eat-me” signal on the cell surface leading to ICD; this cell death was reported to be caspase-dependent on doxorubicin treatment
26
. We observed activation of caspases in the molecular mode of action studies with dapivirine, thus caspase activation and upregulation of calreticulin that we observed in the proteomic analysis could be leading to the loss of viability that we observed in the cellular level studies as well. Further, there are reports on emerging aspects such as ICD, damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPS), and anticancer treatments
27
, wherein, CRT is considered as DAMPS. Also, CRT could play a role in the immunogenicity of cancer cell death
28
. Dapivirine exhibited upregulation of calreticulin in the present study. Thus, it could form an effective treatment option as a chemotherapeutic leading to immunogenic cell death for this aggressive form of cancer.
Ubiquilin-1 was also one of the upregulated entities in the current study. Ubiquilins (UBQLN), belong to the protein family which consists of the ubiquitin-like and ubiquitin-associated domain (UBL-UBA) proteins and function in the proteasome and autophagy pathways. They exhibit diverse functions in cells and cancer
29
. Interestingly, microRNAs (miRNAs), known for their pivotal role in eukaryotic gene expression interact with UBQLN. The miRNAs also contribute to central biological processes including immunity. In breast cancer, miRNAs play critical roles as well
30
. It has been reported that in the in vivo experiments, the miRNA termed, mir-200c is capable of binding to the 3’-UTR of UBQLN1. Further, the overexpression of mir-200c in MDA-MB-231 cells has been shown to lead to a significant decrease in UBQLN1 mRNA levels resulting in radiosensitivity of these cells
31
. Thus, overexpression of mir-200c in cells that are treated with dapivirine could possibly lead to radiosensitivity of this aggressive form of cancer and could be considered under combination therapy.
With respect to treatment for breast cancers, more than 70% of patients receive chemotherapy, but the response rate is low and improvement in response rate is crucial for effective therapy; tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase is reported to sensitize chemotherapeutic agents like docetaxel
32
. In the quest for biomarkers for clinical diagnosis as well as for treatment, transfer RNA fragments (tRFs) have been identified as potential molecules
33
. Further, in TNBC, tryptophan-tRNA ligase (also termed tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase) is reported to be a protein signature molecule for prognosis
34
. Interestingly, this entity is involved in major signaling pathways related to p53 phosphorylation and IFN gamma signaling
35
. Therefore, the upregulation of tryptophan-tRNA ligase cytoplasmic could affect major signaling pathways.
In breast cancer, the basal and luminal types of cells can be distinguished by the types of keratins expressed in these cells
36
. Further, in epithelial cancer cells, loss of keratin 8 and 18 is reported to increase migration of these cells
37
. In the present study, in the dapivirine-treated MDA-MB-231 cells, Keratin Type II cytoskeletal 8 was upregulated. Thus, increased amounts of keratin Type II cytoskeletal 8 could possibly aid in a better prognosis of this aggressive form of cancer.
Actin cytoplasmic 2 was also one of the upregulated entities in the present study. An important role is played by cytoplasmic actin in cancers as well; it could have a role in cell transformation by communicating with nuclear actin of a cell
38
. If resistance arises, compounds that are reported to act on the cytoskeleton in other cancers like glioblastoma
39
, could be considered as combination therapy with dapivirine.
Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A1 (hnRNP A1) belongs to the family of hnRNPs. This protein plays a role in inhibiting splicing by binding to the target RNA
40
. Importantly, it is reported that overexpression of this entity leads to tumor invasion and is an indicator of poor prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma
41
. Importantly, knockdown of hnRNP A1 in MDA-MB-231 cells resulted in significant cell death and inhibited cell invasion as well
42
. Downregulation of hnRNP A1 was observed in the present study on treating MDA-MB-231 cells with dapivirine, thus administration of this drug could be beneficial in preventing invasion of this aggressive form of cancer.
Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) is one of the vital components of the replication machinery of cells and is also involved in DNA repair. In particular, cancer cells exhibit DNA replication that is not regulated, unlimited proliferating potential, and metastasis
43
. Therefore, this entity plays a central role in the process of carcinogenesis. Further, there are reports of cancer cells including breast cancers evading immune surveillance through phosphorylation of nuclear PCNA
44
. Furthermore, in TNBC, EGFR/PCNA targeted through cell-penetrating peptides suppressed tumor growth
45
. In the current study, dapivirine downregulated the key molecule PCNA, which could lead to a significant outcome in inhibiting the proliferation potential of TNBC.
The proteasome activator complex subunit 3 is a component of the proteasome family. Employing unbiased siRNA screening strategy in TNBC cells, it has been reported that the basal type of cells as well as tumor-initiating cells (T-ICs) within the basal type exhibit dependency on proteasomes. Further, inhibiting proteasomes by the clinical inhibitor bortezomib, leads to the suppression of growth as well as metastasis of these cells; notably, inhibition of the function of T-ICs (by the in vitro surrogate assay) including inhibition of tumor initiation has been reported on treatment with the proteasome inhibitor
46
. Importantly, there are no effective therapies that target T-ICs as they are recalcitrant to many chemotherapeutic drugs and are known to be the cause of relapse and recurrence of tumors
47
. Therefore, the study with the clinical inhibitor of proteasome, bortezomib impacting T-ICs of TNBC highlights the importance of this category of inhibitors
46
. Importantly, in the present study, dapivirine downregulated the component, proteasome activator complex subunit 3 in MDA-MB-231 cells. Thus, treatment with dapivirine leading to its impact on the proteasome pathway on which the tumor-initiating cells are dependent upon, could also be considered under novel strategies to combat triple negative breast cancer.
Glutathione S-transferase P (GSTP) has been identified as a novel therapeutic target in TNBC cells by a chemoproteomic based reactivity platform and its inhibition could control TNBC cell growth through metabolic and signaling pathways
48
. Dapivirine treatment of MDA-MB-231 cells did upregulate glutathione S-transferase P. As GSTP is involved in varied phases of cancer progression including development of drug resistance, discovery of inhibitors of GSTP could aid in regulation of the neoplastic process
49
.
BH3-interacting domain death agonist (BID) was among one of the downregulated molecules in the present study. BID plays a role in the process of apoptosis. The apoptosis that we observed in the molecular level analysis could be due to other pathways and not through the BH3 interacting domain. If resistance arises BH3 mimetics could be co-administered
50
.
Calmodulin-2 is an important regulator of calcium and is involved in cell proliferation, invasion and metastasis in various cancers
51
. Elevated expression of Calmodulin-2 has been correlated with invasiveness and metastasis in TNBC and ovarian cancer
52
. Dapivirine downregulated calmodulin-2 in MDA-MB-231 cells. Thus, administration of dapivirine could have potential beneficial effects as a treatment option for TNBC.
60S acidic ribosomal protein P1 (RPLP1) is a component of the ribosomes and is reported to be overexpressed in cancers
53
. Further, it is reported that RPLP1 is elevated in TNBC and is one of the causes of metastasis of this aggressive form of cancer
54
. Notably, RPLP1 was downregulated in dapivirine-treated MDA-MB-231 cells in the current investigation, which could possibly lead to inhibition of metastasis of TNBC.
Stathmin was one of the molecules downregulated as well in the present study. Stathmin belongs to the microtubule dynamic destabilizing protein family. It is overexpressed in pancreatic cancer and it is reported that knockdown of stathmin leads to a decrease in cell viability and colony formation, apart from other effects, and also is a predictor of poor prognosis
55
. In breast cancer, high levels of stathmin are reported to lead to increased cell proliferation and could also contribute towards angiogenesis and immune response of these cells
56
. We observed inhibition of cell proliferation in the cellular level studies, and downregulation of stathmin that we observed by protein profiling could be one of the factors responsible for this. Thus, treatment with dapivirine could have a beneficial effect as a chemotherapeutic treatment for TNBC.
Superoxide dismutase (Cu-Zn) also termed SOD1was one of the components downregulated by dapivirine. SOD1 functions in converting superoxide to hydrogen peroxide. It has been reported that SOD1 could be considered as a target for inhibiting cancer as it is present in various types of cancers
57
. We envision that the downregulation of this key entity in the present study could be beneficial in the treatment of TNBC as it has few treatment options.
Cofilin-1 was also one among the entities upregulated in the present study. Overexpression of cofilin-1 has been reported in several cancers including TNBC. Interestingly, in other cancer cell systems it is reported that its overexpression counteracts invasion
58
. Further, in the cofilin pathway, many entities have been reported to control invasion and not by a single gene like cofilin
59
. Furthermore, active (dephosphorylated) cofilin is reported to affect the release of cytochrome C, therefore, the role of cofilin in the apoptotic pathway is also a major focus in the treatment of cancer
60
. Thus, cofilin could serve as a viable novel therapeutic target for TNBC.
Prelamin-A/C was upregulated in MDA-MB-231 cells on treatment with dapivirine in the current investigation. It has been reported that prelamin-A/C is processed to lamin A/C and its role in different cancer cell types could vary
61
. However, it is reported that in breast cancer, loss of its expression could lead to poor prognosis and shorter survival
62
. Thus, the upregulation of prelamin-A/C that we observed in the present study may have better survival outcomes for patients with TNBC.
Basic transcription factor 3 (BTF3) plays a central role in cancer and is identified as an oncogenic transcription factor in luminal breast cancer
63
. Importantly, it is reported to control stemness and is involved in the immune evasion of these cells in relation to the type I interferon signaling pathway. Knockdown of BTF3 in TNBC has revealed a link between stem-like properties and immune modulation
64
. In the current study, BTF3 was downregulated. Thus, downregulation of this central molecule that could regulate the properties of stem cells and assist in immune attack of this very aggressive form of cancer, could be a highly desired property of an efficacious therapeutic for a cancer like TNBC.
Histone H2AX is a pivotal component of DNA repair. Anticancer agents elicit an increase in reactive oxygen species (ROS) which is reported to lead to cross-talk with histone H2AX. Actually, a decrease in histone H2AX through an increase in ROS is reported to be indicative of increased chemotherapeutic response and better survival of TNBC patients
65
. In the current molecular mode of action analysis, dapivirine elicited an increase in ROS, and on protein profiling, a decrease in histone H2AX was observed. Thus, we envision effective chemotherapeutic response and better survival of TNBC patients when treated with dapivirine.
Programmed cell death protein 5 is implicated in apoptosis in various tumors upon different stimuli and is reported to be cell-type dependent
66
. Downregulation of programmed cell death protein 5 was observed in dapivirine-treated cells. However, in the molecular studies, apoptosis was observed. As various pathways regulate apoptosis, other entities could be involved in the apoptosis that we observed in the current study, for example, we observed upregulation of calreticulin, which is reported to lead to caspase-dependent cell death
26
. We did observe an increase in MultiCaspase as well as executioner caspases 3/7 in the molecular level studies.
Small nuclear ribonucleoprotein F was downregulated in the current study. Small nuclear ribonucleoproteins function in the process of splicing. Due to the process of oncogenesis, many tumors exhibit differential regulation of RNA splicing
67
and respond to spliceosome-triggered therapy. In TNBC, spliceosome-triggered therapy leads to antiviral immune response and apoptosis via the extrinsic pathway
68
. Thus, a decrease in small nuclear ribonucleoprotein F that was observed on dapivirine treatment in the current proteomic analysis could have activated the extrinsic apoptotic pathway which we observed in the molecular level analysis. Further, it could aid in targeting TNBC via an immune response in patients.
In conclusion, the multi-level analysis conducted with dapivirine showed that it could form a potent inhibitor of TNBC as it impacted pivotal cell pathways including the programmed cell death pathway. Further, it has been reported that cell types of TNBC, especially the cells with invasive properties have expression of cell pathways related to the interaction of the ECM-receptor, process of angiogenesis, and cell adhesion
10
. Molecules affecting these metastatic pathways could be considered as a desired option for the treatment of TNBC. Furthermore, as cytotoxic agents have not been efficacious, detecting novel entities by protein profiling is considered as one of the strategies to pursue novel drug development to combat the metastatic potential of TNBC cells
10
. In the present study, dapivirine impacted entities functioning at various levels: ECM, immunomodulation, cell adhesion and angiogenesis. Notably, impact of dapivirine on key cell replication/repair entities like PCNA and H2AX as well as on stem-like cells by downregulation of the transcription factor BTF 3 and the proteasome pathway in MDA-MB-231 cells could possibly lead to efficacious treatment and form a novel strategy to combat the survival of TNBC cells. Even though MDA-MB-231 cell line is the widely used model system for TNBC, to determine the generality of the effects of dapivirine, future studies should include other TNBC cells. Moreover, in a quest for improved treatment strategies for TNBC, antibody-drug conjugates (ADC) have also been employed as novel treatment options as recently described
9
. As dapivirine is not highly bioavailable, it could be administered as ADC or could be embedded in nanoparticles. Of noteworthy, is that dapivirine is approved for the treatment of HIV in certain African countries, thus it could have a beneficial role in combating dual ailments, HIV and TNBC in these individuals. Moreover, we envision that if the outcome with the clinical trials become successful, dapivirine could form an effective treatment option for TNBC.
Methods
Cell lines and materials
Dapivirine was purchased from Selleckchem (Houston, TX, USA). A 50 mM stock solution was prepared in DMSO and stored at – 20 °C until use. Reagents for flow cytometry were purchased from Cytek Biosciences (Fremont, CA, USA).
MDA-MB-231 cell line was purchased from American Type Culture Collection (ATCC, USA). MDA-MB-231 cells were grown in L-15 medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin and 2 mM glutamine. Cultures were incubated at 37 °C in the absence of CO
2
. MCF-7 and MCF 10A cell lines were also purchased from ATCC. MCF-7 cells were cultured in Eagle’s minimal essential medium (EMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin (P/S) and 2 mM glutamine. MCF 10A cells were grown in DMEM/F12 supplemented with 5% horse serum, EGF (20 ng/ml), Hydrocortisone (0.5 µg/ml), Insulin (10 µg/ml), Non-essential amino acids (1%) and P/S (1%). Both MCF-7 and MCF 10A cell lines were maintained at 37 °C in a 5% CO
2
atmosphere.
Assessment of the effect of dapivirine on the viability of MDA-MB-231 cells
The assays were performed as described earlier
69
. Essentially, MDA-MB-231 cells were plated in 96-well plates at a density of 5000 cells per well. After 24 h, cells were treated with varying concentrations of dapivirine in triplicates and incubated for 72 h at 37 °C. Cell viability was assessed by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) (Bimake, Houston, TX, USA). The media was aspirated, and 200 µL of 20% CCK-8 solution in the complete growth medium was added. Absorbance was measured at 450 nm using an Infinite 200Pro plate reader (Tecan, USA) after 1.5 h of incubation at 37 °C. The viability of cells was expressed after normalizing the treatment group absorbance values to that of the control group. Using Prism software, version 7.0 (GraphPad, USA), graphs were generated and IC
50
was determined. Three independent experiments were performed.
Immunofluorescence labelling
Cells were plated in glass chamber slides at a density of 20,000 cells/well. After 24 h, they were treated with 1 µM, 2 µM and 5 µM of dapivirine for 72 h. Thereafter, cells were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde for 10 min and washed twice with PBS, each for a minute. Cells were permeabilized with 0.1% Triton X-100 for 5 min followed by application of fluorescent labeled phalloidin (Actin Red 555 ReadyProbes Reagent, Invitrogen
R37112
) for 10 min at room temperature as per manufacturer’s instructions and washed twice in PBS for 1 min each time.
Clonogenic assays
These assays were performed essentially as described earlier
69
. MDA-MB-231 cells treated with varying concentrations of dapivirine were trypsinized and replated at a density of 500 cells/well in 6-well plates in the growth medium. Cells from untreated cultures served as controls. The assays were done in triplicates. After 10 days of incubation, cultures were fixed and stained with crystal violet. Quantitative estimation was made by lysing the colonies by adding 1% SDS and measuring the absorbance at 590 nm.
Flow cytometric analysis
Flow cytometric assays were performed essentially as described
70
. MDA-MB-231 cells were plated in 12-well plates at 62,500 cells/well. After 24 h, cultures were treated in triplicate for 72 h with 1 µM, 2 µM and 5 µM concentrations of dapivirine. Cultures with only media served as controls. After 72 h of incubation, cultures were trypsinized and cells were pooled together from triplicate treatments before proceeding with flow cytometry assay kit protocol as per manufacturer’s instructions (Cytek Biosciences, Fremont, CA, USA). The following Luminex Muse assay kits were used: Oxidative Stress kit (MCH100111), Annexin V and dead cell kit (MCH100105), MultiCaspase kit (MCH100109), Caspases 3/7 (MCH100108).
Proteomic analysis
Protein profiling was performed by first running 2-D DIGE, followed by Mass spectrometry by Applied Biomics Inc. (Hayward, CA, USA). Basically, the following procedures were employed for the protein profiling. Cells were plated (62,000 cells/well) in 12-well plates. Cells were treated at 3.5 µM dapivirine and untreated controls were maintained in parallel. After 72 h, cells from control samples and treated samples were collected, washed with 1× PBS, and then stored at −  80 °C prior to sending the samples to Applied Biomics, Inc (Hayward, CA, USA) on dry ice for proteomic analysis. The protocol performed was as described previously
70
–
72
. STRING database version 12.0 was used to perform functional enrichment analysis and to generate protein-protein interaction networks
73
.
